findings.issue: Line 1 makes the discrete-versus-continuous step unconditional, potentially implying that categorical variables also receive that classification.
findings.evidence: SOURCE limits the second step with "then (if quantitative) discrete-vs-continuous"; PROPOSED says only "then discrete or continuous."

findings.issue: Line 2 changes the point-loss condition by presenting any comparison of charts with mismatched axes as the error.
findings.evidence: SOURCE identifies comparing charts on different scales "without noticing" the mismatch; PROPOSED says "comparing charts whose axes don't match," omitting that essential condition. A comparison that accounts for the different scales is not the described error.

findings.issue: Line 1 adds an unsupported exclusivity claim about which displays can show modality.
findings.evidence: SOURCE says modality cannot be read from a boxplot and can be described directly on a histogram or dotplot. PROPOSED strengthens this to "modality is visible only on a histogram or dotplot," excluding other displays without source support.
